text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

At the end of June the Rebhalde Cooperative told me that my rent is going up. According to their notice of 29 June 2026, the rent for my flat at Rosenweg 54 in Wohlen will go from CHF 3270 to CHF 3350 a month from 1 October 2026. For our household that is a noticeable jump on top of everything else getting more expensive.

My lease, which I signed in December 2022, contains a clause tying the rent to the Swiss consumer price index, and this increase applies that index clause. The notice gives the old and the new index figure.

The cooperative does not say anywhere that its own costs have gone up, and there has been no renovation or other work on the building. The only reason the notice gives is the change in the index.

I've attached the notice so you can see it for yourself.

What confuses me is that the lease is a bit of a muddle. On another page there is a table saying the rent goes up by fixed amounts on certain dates. Whether this increase is also one of those steps, I honestly can't work out. My friend Nina Fankhauser, who read the contract with me, is fairly sure it is, because the date matches the table. When I asked Mr Felix Frei, he said the table was "no longer relevant" but wouldn't explain why. So that part is still a mystery to me.

Could you help me understand whether this increase is correct? I'd like to know if I should contest it before any deadline runs out.

Thank you,
Emma Brunner

NOTIFICATION OF RENT INCREASE
Official form approved by the Canton of Aargau

Tenant: Emma Brunner
Property: 4.5-room flat, Rosenweg 54, Wohlen

Previous rent: CHF 3270 per month
New rent: CHF 3350 per month
Effective from: 1 October 2026

Reason: Adjustment of the rent under the index clause of the lease agreement of 24 December 2022 to the change in the Swiss consumer price index.
Swiss consumer price index (December 2020 = 100): previous value 104.2, new value 106.9

If you do not agree with the increase, you may contest it with the conciliation authority within 30 days of receipt.

Wohlen, 29 June 2026
Rebhalde Cooperative
Felix Frei
